metadata.title: Palantir raises full-year outlook after third-quarter revenue jumps 96%

content.text:
Palantir Technologies Inc (NYSE:PLTR) lifted its full-year financial outlook after reporting third-quarter revenue growth of 96%, with strong demand for its artificial intelligence software driving gains across its US commercial and government businesses.
The data analytics and AI software company generated revenue of $2.31 billion for the three months ended September 30, beating analyst expectations of $2.18 billion. Revenue was up 96% from the same period last year.
Adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.44, ahead of the $0.41 consensus estimate, while adjusted operating income reached $1.43 billion, compared with expectations of $1.26 billion.
US commercial revenue was a standout, climbing 148% year over year to $984 million, ahead of estimates of $943 million. US government revenue rose 96% to $953 million, also exceeding expectations of $862 million.
Total US revenue increased 119% to $1.94 billion.
Following the results, Palantir raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $8.530 billion to $8.534 billion, above analyst expectations of approximately $8.2 billion.
The company now expects adjusted operating income of between $5.245 billion and $5.249 billion, compared with the $4.76 billion consensus, while adjusted free cash flow is forecast at $4.8 billion to $5 billion, ahead of estimates of $4.52 billion.
Palantir also expects US commercial revenue to exceed $3.6 billion for the year.
For the fourth quarter, the company forecast revenue of $2.649 billion to $2.653 billion, comfortably above analyst expectations of $2.46 billion. Adjusted operating income is expected to reach between $1.64 billion and $1.644 billion, compared with the $1.41 billion consensus.
Operating performance remained strong in the third quarter, with an adjusted operating margin of 62% and a Rule of 40 score of 158%.
Total contract value reached $2.92 billion, up 6% year over year. US commercial total contract value increased 11% to $1.46 billion, while US commercial remaining deal value climbed 79% to $6.52 billion.
Palantir closed 212 deals worth at least $1 million during the quarter, including 107 deals of at least $5 million and 64 worth $10 million or more.
CEO Alex Karp pointed to the growing divide between organizations adopting artificial intelligence and those falling behind.
"The Sovereign AI movement is imposing the most dramatic dichotomy between haves and have nots that I have witnessed in 30 years of business," Karp said.
"Every institution—government and commercial—is rapidly being forced, voluntarily or not, into one of these two categories."
